title: SambaNova SN40L: Scaling the AI Memory Wall with Dataflow and Composition of Experts
problem: Modern AI accelerators exhibit compute-to-memory imbalance creating a memory wall that makes efficiently deploying large language models challenging. Composition of Experts approaches reduce model size but suffer from lower operational intensity and expensive dynamic model switching on conventional hardware.
motivation: Monolithic LLM deployment at scale remains prohibitively expensive and complex, making modular approaches with specialized hardware necessary for practical enterprise AI deployment.
method: The paper introduces Samba-CoE, a composition of 150 expert models (1 trillion parameters total) deployed on the SambaNova SN40L Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit. The RDU combines streaming dataflow execution with a three-tier memory hierarchy (on-chip SRAM, on-package HBM, off-package DDR DRAM) and fused operations to improve operational intensity. A dedicated inter-RDU network enables scaling across multiple sockets.
key_novelty: Codesigned combination of Composition of Experts with streaming dataflow architecture and three-tier memory hierarchy to overcome the AI memory wall for practical LLM deployment.
contributions: Samba-CoE system with 150 expert models totaling 1 trillion parameters for modular LLM inference and training
SambaNova SN40L RDU architecture with three-tier memory system and dataflow-based execution enabling efficient expert model switching
Demonstrated 2-13x speedups on various benchmarks with 19x reduction in machine footprint
Achieved 3.7x speedup over DGX H100 and 6.6x speedup over DGX A100 on CoE inference

metrics.speedup: 2-13x on benchmarks, 3.7x vs DGX H100, 6.6x vs DGX A100
metrics.other: 19x reduction in machine footprint, 15-31x speedup in model switching
